tasks.title: Build the flags-document generator over a flag.FlagSet
steps: Write TS-09-14 through TS-09-21 in a new internal/toolio/flagschema_test.go and confirm they fail
Add internal/toolio/flagschema.go defining an ordered schema node type (a slice of {name, node} pairs) with a custom MarshalJSON, so property order never goes through Go's sorted map-key marshalling
Implement BuildFlagsDocument(fs *flag.FlagSet) that walks fs.VisitAll in its existing name order, skipping the flags named "schema" and "version"

For each remaining flag, set description from f.Usage verbatim; when f.Value implements flag.Getter, infer type from Get()'s dynamic type (string, bool, int64, float64 -> string/boolean/integer/number) and set default from the flag's own default; special-case time.Duration as {type: string, format: duration} with default rendered via the duration's String(); when Value does not implement flag.Getter, report {type: string} with default from f.Value.String()

Add a small registry, e.g. func DeclareEnum(fs *flag.FlagSet, name string, values []string), pairing an already-registered flag with its closed set of legal values (Design Decision 7); have BuildFlagsDocument add an enum key only for a flag so declared
Wrap the result as {"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "type": "object", "properties": {...}}, with no required and no additionalProperties key
In cmd/fix/main.go and cmd/impl/main.go, call toolio.DeclareEnum(fs, "land", codefix.LandModes) / codeimpl.LandModes immediately after each tool's --land StringVar registration
Run TS-09-14 through TS-09-21 against fix's fully-populated FlagSet (including --pull) and iterate until green

tasks.title: Build the reflection-based result-document generator and tag every reachable field
steps: Write TS-09-22 through TS-09-28 in a new internal/toolio/resultschema_test.go and confirm they fail

Add internal/toolio/resultschema.go reusing the ordered-node schema type from flagschema.go (factor the shared type and its MarshalJSON into a small internal/toolio/schemadoc.go if that keeps both files simple)

Implement SchemaFor(t reflect.Type) that turns a struct into {type: object, properties: ..., required: ...} using reflect.VisibleFields (so an anonymously embedded struct's fields are promoted in place), a slice into {type: array, items: <element schema>}, a pointer into its pointee's own schema with no separate nullable marker, and a scalar into the matching JSON Schema primitive
Read each field's json tag exactly as encoding/json does: the tag's name and omitempty decide the property name and required-ness, and json:"-" skips the field entirely
Add a new `description` struct tag read alongside `json`, and set every generated property's description from it

Add the `description` tag to every exported, JSON-tagged field in: internal/toolio/envelope.go (Envelope, InputInfo, ModelInfo, UsageInfo, PhaseInfo, ErrorInfo), codefix/types.go (Result, FileChange, Analysis, Ambiguity, Implementation) and codefix/criteria.go (Criterion, CriterionVerdict), codeimpl/types.go (Result, TaskReport, Survey, Location, Drift, Blocker, Submission, RepairSubmission, RepairReport, GateResult, FileChange, Verdict), issuetriage/pipeline.go (Result) and issuetriage/issue.go (FileRef, Fix), internal/checks/checks.go (Result), specgen/pipeline.go (Result, Package, ScopeReport, ValidationReport, ValidationItem, TraceReport, OpenQuestion)

Implement BuildResultDocument(sample any) that calls SchemaFor(reflect.TypeOf(toolio.Envelope{})) and substitutes the Envelope.Result property's schema with SchemaFor(reflect.TypeOf(sample)), wrapping the whole thing as {"$schema": "…/2020-12/schema", "type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...]}
Run TS-09-22 through TS-09-28 against specgen.Result (to exercise the embedded Package promotion) and against codefix.Result and toolio.Envelope, and iterate until green
